title: Error tracking issue writes: which mutations emit lifecycle events
answers: Which issue mutations must emit lifecycle events?
Where are error tracking issue write paths?
When are $error_tracking_issue_* events emitted and when not?
Why must events be registered inside the transaction?
body:
Write paths: `logic/issue_mutations.py:update_issue|merge_issues|split_issue|assign_issue|bulk_update_issues|_assign_one|set_issue_cohort`, re-exported by `facade/issues.py`. Pattern: PG write -> `log_activity` -> register lifecycle events -> stamp `state_updated_at` -> ClickHouse sync on commit.
- Emit: status change to active/resolved/suppressed (`lifecycle_events.py:STATUS_CHANGE_EVENTS`, also bulk `set_status`); `_assign_one` set -> ISSUE_ASSIGNED_EVENT, clear -> ISSUE_UNASSIGNED_EVENT; `merge_issues` only when result is MERGED -> ISSUE_MERGED_EVENT; `split_issue` only if new issues created -> ISSUE_SPLIT_EVENT.
- No event for no-ops (`_assign_one` returns None: no event/log/stamp/CH sync; bulk skips issues already in target status). No events for severity/name/description changes, `set_issue_cohort`, or merge adopting a source assignee (`models.py:_adopt_source_assignee_on_merge`, silent).
- Events are snapshotted via `prepare_issue_lifecycle_event` inside the transaction (merge sources get deleted) and published by `produce_issue_lifecycle_events_on_commit` (`transaction.on_commit(robust=True)`); registration must be inside the txn so a CH sync failure does not lose the event (retry sees no transition).
- One team per batch (ValueError otherwise). Producer/celery failures are swallowed/logged, never fail the mutation.
- Bulk actions pass `opener_allowed=False`: `_with_reply_targets` drops transitions unless an `ErrorTrackingAlertThread` already exists.
- Ingestion transitions (created, reopened-by-exception, spiking) come from cymbal, not Django. Manual reopen reuses the cymbal ISSUE_REOPENED_EVENT.
applies: Django-side user-driven mutations only; ingestion-driven events are produced by cymbal (Rust), not verified here.
